title: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
seo_title: Semiconductor Electronics Class 12 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 14)
standard_text: Energy bands in conductors, semiconductors and insulators (qualitative ideas only). Intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors – p and n type, p-n junction. Semiconductor diode – I–V characteristics in forward and reverse bias, application of junction diode – diode as a rectifier.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 14 Semiconductor Electronics: energy bands, intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, doping, the p-n junction, diode bias and rectifiers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: n-type: extra electrons (group 15 dopant); p-type: holes (group 13 dopant).
key_sub: A diode conducts in forward bias, not reverse.
body_html:
How to think about it

Conductors have overlapping bands, insulators a large gap and semiconductors a small gap (silicon about 1.1 eV). A pure (intrinsic) semiconductor has equal electrons and holes, ne = nh = ni. Doping with a group 15 element (arsenic) gives n-type; with a group 13 element (boron) gives p-type; always nenh = ni².

A p-n junction forms a depletion region and a barrier (about 0.7 V for silicon). Forward bias narrows it and current flows; reverse bias widens it. Diodes rectify AC: a half-wave rectifier gives one pulse per cycle and a full-wave rectifier two.

Example

Si doped with boron?

group 13

Answer: p-type

Example

Full-wave, 50 Hz input?

2 × 50

Answer: 100 Hz ripple

Common mistakes

  • Saying n-type is negatively charged.
  • Swapping forward and reverse bias.
  • Using the input frequency for a full-wave ripple.

faq.q: What is the difference between n-type and p-type semiconductors?
faq.a: n-type has extra electrons from group 15 donors; p-type has holes from group 13 acceptors.

faq.q: Why does a p-n junction rectify?
faq.a: It conducts easily in forward bias but hardly at all in reverse bias.

items.q: What happens to the depletion layer under reverse bias?
items.e: Only a tiny reverse current flows.
